ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Swami Vivekananda — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Review after seven months away and a week after an asthma attack: A1c, kidneys, lipids, spirometry with bronchodilator response and FeNO; asthma and diabetic kidney disease confirmed; empagliflozin and maintenance-and-reliever inhaler; fasting plan for the coming festival

text.paragraph: Review after seven months away, a week after an asthma attack. [S]

Swami Vivekananda returns a week after the sick visit for a moderate asthma attack, and nine days after coming home from seven months of travel in the mountains. He finished five days of prednisone three days ago; his glucose rose to 210 to 268 mg/dL before the evening meal during the course and came back to 120 to 140 fasting within two days, without other treatment. The nurse telephoned on the second day. He has used the budesonide-formoterol inhaler two to four times a day; he has woken twice in the week with tightness, and the attacks are milder. While away he took metformin 1872 mg, losartan and atorvastatin, messaged his fasting readings (110 to 135 mg/dL), and kept his fortnightly fasts with fruit and milk. He could not find a laboratory for the three-month blood tests, so they were not done. He completed four of six video sessions for insomnia and falls asleep within about 45 minutes on most nights. The festival of the goddess is in two weeks and he intends to keep its fast. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1898-10-27; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; weight 74.8 kg, BMI 25.3; blood pressure 126/78, pulse 82; oxygen saturation 97 percent
Faint expiratory wheeze on forced expiration
Skin intact after months of walking; no calluses or sores

Thirst, frequent urination day and night, tiredness and about 4 kg weight loss over two months, with a random glucose of 246 mg/dL; told by physicians a year ago that he had diabetes, never confirmed with modern tests or treated except by diet. Diabetes to be confirmed and classified (type 2, type 1 or slowly progressive autoimmune diabetes) with A1c, fasting glucose, GAD antibodies and C-peptide
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to his documented diabetes of the year before. Superseded by the diagnosis at the second visit.

Type 2 diabetes: A1c 9.4 percent and fasting glucose 172 mg/dL, with symptoms; GAD65 antibodies negative and fasting C-peptide preserved (2.6 ng/mL); no ketones. BMI 24.6, in the range where ADA screens Asian Americans. Classified as type 2, not type 1 or slowly progressive autoimmune diabetes
S — Synthetic modern confirmation and classification linked to his documented diabetes.

S — Synthetic finding linked to his documented albuminuria; superseded when diabetic kidney disease was confirmed.

S — Synthetic finding; not a claim about his real blood pressure.

S — Synthetic finding of the modern episode; not a claim about his real blood pressure, which was never recorded.

Long-standing difficulty falling asleep: by his own account he has never been able to fall asleep on getting into bed and lies awake for two hours or more most nights; worse lately with waking to pass urine; rises before dawn for meditation
S — Synthetic modern problem linked to his documented lifelong difficulty falling asleep.
Mixed hyperlipidemia: LDL cholesterol 132 mg/dL, triglycerides 228, HDL 36

Attacks of wheeze and breathlessness for three weeks since coming down from the mountains to the damp plains, the worst last night with a sense of suffocation: peak flow 330 L/min (56 percent of predicted), oxygen saturation 94 percent, rising to 410 L/min after bronchodilator; no fever, edema or chest pain; chest X-ray and ECG without heart failure or pneumonia. Asthma to be confirmed with spirometry
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to his documented suffocating attacks of asthma on his return to Belur. Superseded by the diagnosis a week later.

Asthma, adult onset, confirmed: FEV1 2.95 L (77 percent predicted) rising 470 mL (16 percent) after bronchodilator, FEV1/FVC 0.66 rising to 0.75; FeNO 44 ppb; brought on by damp air and smoke; one moderate attack treated with prednisone
S — Synthetic modern confirmation linked to his documented attacks of asthma.
Diabetic kidney disease, CKD stage G1 A2: moderately increased albuminuria on three samples over eight months (46, 41 and 34 mg/g) with eGFR above 90
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis linked to his documented albuminuria and Bright's disease; not a claim about the cause of his real kidney disease.

list.item:
Asthma, adult onset, confirmed (J45.40). Asthma is confirmed: FEV1/FVC 0.66 rises to 0.75 after albuterol, with a 470 mL (16 percent) rise in FEV1, and FeNO 44 ppb shows type 2 inflammation. It began on his return to the damp plains and is not controlled (Asthma Control Test 15, night waking, a recent attack needing prednisone), so he needs maintenance treatment, not only a reliever. Read with race-neutral equations, his FEV1 is 77 percent of predicted. [S]
GINA track 1, step 3: budesonide-formoterol one inhalation twice daily and one as needed, up to 12 a day, with a spacer.
Written action plan; peak flow meter to set his personal best.
Smoke-free room; incense outside where he can.
Review in four to six weeks; repeat spirometry in three months.

Diabetic kidney disease, G1 A2 (E11.21). Moderately increased albuminuria on three samples over eight months (46, 41 and 34 mg/g) with an eGFR of 103 confirms diabetic kidney disease, stage G1 A2. It has fallen with better glucose and losartan, but persists. An SGLT2 inhibitor protects the kidneys and the heart and lowers glucose without hypoglycemia. He agreed to start it now, with clear rules for fasting and illness. [S]
Empagliflozin 10 mg each morning.
Skip empagliflozin on any day of fasting without water, and stop it and metformin when unable to eat or drink; drink well on fruit-and-milk fast days.
Watch for genital itching or soreness; keep the area clean.
Potassium, creatinine and urine albumin in three months, then every six months.

Type 2 diabetes, at target (E11.65). A1c 6.9 percent on metformin, down from 9.4; prednisone raised his evening glucose briefly, as expected. The A1c due at three months was missed while he travelled. [S]
Continue metformin 1872 mg and add empagliflozin as above.
For the festival fast: metformin with the meal that ends the fast; empagliflozin taken on fruit-and-milk fast days but skipped on a waterless day; glucose at midday and before breaking the fast; break it if below 70 or above 300 mg/dL, or if dizzy or unwell.
A1c in three months.

Continue losartan 25 mg.

Continue atorvastatin 10 mg; lipids yearly.

Insomnia (G47.00). Better with cognitive behavioral therapy; he wants to finish the course. [S]

Problem resolved.
